html:
The Amu Darya, the ancient Oxus, is the greatest river of Central Asia, about 2,400 km long. It rises in the Pamirs, forms much of Afghanistan's northern border, then crosses the desert of Turkmenistan and Uzbekistan toward the Aral Sea.

For Persians and Greeks it was the line between Iran and the steppe beyond. The Bronze Age Oxus civilisation grew in oases near it. Bactria lay on its upper course and Sogdia across it to the north. Alexander the Great crossed it in 329 BCE, and the Greek city of Ai-Khanoum later stood on its bank. Its delta was the land of Khwarazm, seat of the Khwarazmian Empire that the Mongols smashed in 1220.

In the Soviet era its water was turned onto cotton fields, much of it through the Karakum Canal. So little reached the delta that the Aral Sea began to shrink in the 1960s. Upstream, dams such as Nurek on its tributaries now worry the farmers downstream.
